examples.ko: 그 선수는 실력과 인성을 겸비해서 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: That player has both skill and character, so he is very popular.

examples.ko: 지혜와 용기를 겸비한 사람이 리더가 돼야 해요.
examples.en: A person with both wisdom and courage should become the leader.

examples.ko: 이 회사는 디자인과 기능을 겸비한 제품을 만들어요.
examples.en: This company makes products that combine design and function.

examples.ko: 외모와 실력을 모두 겸비하기는 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It is not easy to have both looks and talent.
She has both talent and virtue, so she is respected.

examples.ko: 이 카페는 맛과 분위기를 모두 겸비했어요.
examples.en: This cafe has both good taste and a good atmosphere.

explain: 보통 'A와 B를 겸비하다'처럼 좋은 점 두 가지 이상을 함께 가졌을 때 칭찬하는 말이에요. 나쁜 점에는 쓰지 않고, '갖추다'보다 글이나 격식 있는 말투에서 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is usually used as 'A와 B를 겸비하다' to praise someone or something for having two or more good qualities together. It is not used for bad qualities, and it sounds more formal or written than '갖추다'.

examples.ko: 두 팀이 우승을 두고 치열한 경합을 벌였어요.
examples.en: The two teams had a fierce contest for the championship.

examples.ko: 여당과 야당이 경합하는 지역이라서 관심이 커요.
examples.en: The ruling and opposition parties are competing in this area, so there is a lot of interest.

examples.ko: 오랜 경합 끝에 우리 회사가 계약을 따냈어요.
examples.en: After a long contest, our company won the contract.

examples.ko: 경합 지역에서는 표 차이가 아주 작아요.
examples.en: In swing districts, the vote gap is very small.
Several companies jumped into the bidding contest.
Competition was so intense that prices dropped a lot.

explain: '경쟁'보다 실력이 비슷한 상대끼리 팽팽하게 맞서는 느낌이 있어요. 선거, 스포츠, 입찰 뉴스에서 '경합을 벌이다', '경합 지역'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: Compared with '경쟁', it suggests evenly matched rivals going head to head. You will see it in election, sports and bidding news in phrases like '경합을 벌이다' and '경합 지역' (swing district).

examples.ko: 모든 학생에게 균등한 기회를 줘야 해요.
examples.en: We must give all students equal opportunities.
I shared the cake equally with my friends.

examples.ko: 교육 기회가 균등하지 않다고 느끼는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people feel that educational opportunities are not equal.

examples.ko: 기회 균등은 우리 사회의 중요한 가치예요.
examples.en: Equal opportunity is an important value in our society.
I checked whether taxes are collected evenly.

examples.ko: 균등 분할로 결제하면 한 달에 오만 원이에요.
examples.en: If you pay in equal installments, it is 50,000 won a month.

explain: '평등'이 사람의 권리나 대우가 같다는 쪽이라면, '균등'은 기회, 몫, 양이 고르게 나뉘는 쪽에 잘 어울려요. '기회균등', '균등하게 나누다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: While '평등' is mostly about equal rights or treatment of people, '균등' fits chances, shares and amounts being spread evenly. Typical uses are '기회균등' and '균등하게 나누다'.

examples.ko: 백제 금동 대향로는 국립부여박물관에서 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can see the Baekje Gilt-bronze Incense Burner at the National Buyeo Museum.

examples.ko: 이 금동 불상은 천 년이 넘었어요.
examples.en: This gilt-bronze Buddha statue is over a thousand years old.

examples.ko: 금동으로 만든 작은 종이 전시돼 있어요.
examples.en: A small bell made of gilt bronze is on display.

examples.ko: 박물관에서 금동 관을 봤는데 정말 화려했어요.
examples.en: I saw a gilt-bronze crown at the museum, and it was really splendid.

examples.ko: 이 박물관에는 금동 유물이 아주 많아요.
examples.en: This museum has many gilt-bronze artifacts.

examples.ko: 금동 장식이 달린 상자를 선물로 받았어요.
examples.en: I received a box with gilt-bronze decorations as a gift.

explain: 주로 박물관과 문화재 설명에서 '금동 불상', '금동 대향로'처럼 다른 명사 앞에 붙어서 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 거의 쓰지 않지만 한국 역사나 여행 이야기에서는 꼭 만나요.
explain_en: It mostly appears in museum and cultural-heritage explanations, placed before another noun, as in '금동 불상' or '금동 대향로'. You rarely use it in everyday talk, but you will meet it when reading about Korean history or travel.

examples.ko: 그 그림은 너무 기괴해서 오래 못 보겠어요.
examples.en: That painting is so grotesque that I can't look at it for long.
I heard a bizarre, eerie sound in the forest at night.

examples.ko: 영화 속 분위기가 기괴하지만 계속 보게 돼요.
examples.en: The mood in the movie is creepy, but I keep watching.

examples.ko: 그 건물의 모양이 기괴하다고 사람들이 말해요.
examples.en: People say that building's shape is bizarre.
The dream I had last night was so weird and creepy.

examples.ko: 기괴하게 생긴 인형이 가게 앞에 있었어요.
examples.en: There was a strange-looking, creepy doll in front of the shop.

explain: '이상하다'보다 훨씬 강해서, 정상이 아니라 불쾌하거나 무서운 느낌이 들 때 써요. 그림, 영화, 소문, 소리처럼 분위기를 말할 때 어울려요.
explain_en: It is much stronger than '이상하다' and gives an uneasy, creepy feeling of something abnormal. It suits things like paintings, films, rumors and sounds.

en: be sold to a bidder; be auctioned

examples.ko: 낙찰된 업체는 열흘 안에 계약서를 내야 해요.
examples.en: The company awarded the bid must submit the contract within ten days.

examples.ko: 우리 팀 제안이 낙찰됐다는 소식에 팀원들이 모두 기뻐했어요.
examples.en: All the team members were happy to hear our proposal had won the bid.
That painting was sold at auction for 200 million won.

examples.ko: 가장 낮은 가격을 낸 곳이 낙찰돼요.
examples.en: The one that offers the lowest price gets the bid.

examples.ko: 어제 온라인 경매에서 시계가 낙찰되지 않았어요.
examples.en: The watch wasn't sold in yesterday's online auction.

examples.ko: 공사가 낙찰되면 바로 일을 시작할 거예요.
examples.en: Once the construction project is awarded, we will start work right away.

explain: 경매에서는 물건이 팔릴 때, 입찰에서는 사업이나 공사가 어느 한 곳으로 정해질 때 써요. 사람이 주어이면 '낙찰받다'를 많이 쓰고, 입찰이 성립하지 않은 경우는 '유찰되다'라고 해요.
explain_en: For auctions it means an item gets sold, and for tenders it means a project is awarded to one bidder. When a person or company is the subject, '낙찰받다' is often used, and a failed tender is '유찰되다'.

en: sell to a bidder; offer a contract

examples.ko: 경매인은 가장 높은 값을 부른 사람에게 낙찰해요.
examples.en: The auctioneer sells the item to the person who called the highest price.

examples.ko: 시에서 이 공사를 한 업체에 낙찰했어요.
examples.en: The city awarded this construction project to one company.
I heard they decided to award it to the lowest bidder.
We plan to award the bid as soon as the review is finished.
I wonder why they awarded the contract to that company.

examples.ko: 점수가 가장 높은 곳에 낙찰하려고 해요.
examples.en: We intend to award it to the one with the highest score.

explain: 물건이나 사업을 넘겨주는 쪽(경매인, 발주처)이 주어예요. 받는 쪽은 '낙찰되다', '낙찰받다'를 쓰고, 넘겨받는 대상에는 '~에 낙찰하다'처럼 조사 '에'를 써요.
explain_en: The subject is the side that hands the item or project over, such as the auctioneer or the ordering organization. The winning side uses '낙찰되다' or '낙찰받다', and the recipient takes the particle '에', as in '~에 낙찰하다'.

examples.ko: 태풍 때문에 섬과의 통신이 이틀째 두절되고 있어요.
examples.en: Because of the typhoon, communication with the island has been cut off for two days.
It snowed a lot, so traffic was cut off.

examples.ko: 그 사람과 연락이 두절된 지 한 달이 됐어요.
examples.en: It has been a month since I lost contact with that person.
If the road is cut off by a landslide, the village gets isolated.
The phone lines were down, so I had no news of my family.

examples.ko: 친구가 연락 두절 상태라서 너무 걱정이에요.
examples.en: My friend is out of contact, so I'm really worried.

explain: 연락, 통신, 교통, 소식처럼 이어져 있어야 할 것이 끊길 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '연락이 끊기다'라고 많이 말하고, '연락 두절'은 뉴스나 공문에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is used when something that should stay connected, such as contact, communication, traffic or news, is cut off. In daily speech people say '연락이 끊기다', while '연락 두절' shows up mostly in news and official notices.

examples.en: Cinderella went to the ball held at the palace.
The school held a ball to celebrate graduation.

examples.ko: 무도회 날 입을 드레스를 새로 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a new dress to wear on the day of the ball.

examples.ko: 영화 속 무도회 장면이 정말 화려했어요.
examples.en: The ball scene in the movie was really gorgeous.
A rumor spread that a ball would be held at the palace.

examples.ko: 무도회에서 처음 만난 두 사람은 금방 친해졌어요.
examples.en: The two people who first met at the ball quickly became close.

explain: 서양식으로 격식 있게 춤추는 모임이라서 옛날이야기, 영화, 동화에 주로 나와요. 한국에서 요즘 친구들끼리 하는 행사는 '파티'나 '댄스 파티'라고 해요.
explain_en: It refers to a formal Western-style dance gathering, so it mainly appears in old stories, films and fairy tales. A modern event among friends in Korea would be called '파티' or '댄스 파티'.

examples.ko: 남은 빚을 다음 달까지 변제해야 해요.
examples.en: I have to pay off the remaining debt by next month.

examples.ko: 일부만 변제해서는 계약을 끝낼 수 없다고 변호사가 알려 줬어요.
examples.en: The lawyer told me I can't end the contract by repaying only part of it.

examples.ko: 그는 오 년에 걸쳐 빚을 모두 변제했어요.
examples.en: He paid off all his debt over five years.
I talked with the bank about how to repay the money.
What do I do if I don't have the money to repay?

examples.ko: 빚을 다 변제하면 신용 등급도 올라가요.
examples.en: Once you pay off all your debt, your credit rating goes up too.

explain: '갚다'와 같은 일이지만 법, 계약, 은행 이야기에서 쓰는 딱딱한 말이에요. 일상에서는 '빚을 갚다'라고 하고, '채무 변제', '변제 기한'처럼 명사로도 많이 나와요.
explain_en: It describes the same act as '갚다' but in a stiff tone used for law, contracts and banking. In daily life people say '빚을 갚다', and the noun appears in phrases like '채무 변제' and '변제 기한'.

examples.ko: 가끔 심장이 불규칙하게 뛰어서 부정맥 검사를 받았어요.
examples.en: My heart sometimes beats irregularly, so I had an arrhythmia test.
My father has an arrhythmia, so he takes medicine.

examples.ko: 부정맥은 심하면 어지러움이 생길 수 있어요.
examples.en: If an arrhythmia is severe, it can cause dizziness.
To treat an arrhythmia, you need to go to the hospital.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 부정맥 증상을 자세히 물어봤어요.
examples.en: The doctor asked me in detail about my arrhythmia symptoms.

examples.ko: 부정맥 환자는 운동 전에 의사와 상담하는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: People with an arrhythmia should talk to a doctor before exercising.

explain: 병원에서는 '부정맥이 있다', '부정맥 진단을 받다'처럼 말해요. 병명을 모를 때는 '가슴이 두근거려요', '맥박이 불규칙해요'처럼 증상으로 설명할 수도 있어요.
explain_en: At the hospital you say '부정맥이 있다' or '부정맥 진단을 받다'. If you do not know the name, you can describe the symptoms instead, such as '가슴이 두근거려요' or '맥박이 불규칙해요'.

examples.ko: 이 옷은 한쪽 소매만 길어서 디자인이 비대칭이에요.
examples.en: Only one sleeve of this outfit is long, so the design is asymmetrical.
I was worried because I was told my face is asymmetrical.
The asymmetrical building is a landmark of the city.

examples.ko: 두 나라의 군사력은 비대칭이라서 협상이 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: The two countries' military strength is asymmetrical, so negotiations are not easy.
Asymmetrical hairstyles are popular these days.

examples.ko: 자세가 나쁘면 몸이 비대칭으로 변할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Bad posture can make your body become asymmetrical.

explain: 반대말은 '대칭'이에요. 얼굴, 몸, 디자인처럼 모양뿐 아니라 '정보 비대칭'처럼 힘이나 정보의 차이가 고르지 않을 때도 써요.
explain_en: The opposite is '대칭'. Besides shapes such as faces, bodies and designs, it is also used for uneven power or information, as in '정보 비대칭'.

examples.en: The government decided to increase its rice reserves.

examples.ko: 겨울이 오기 전에 연료 비축이 필요해요.
examples.en: We need to stock up on fuel before winter comes.

examples.ko: 비축 물량이 충분해서 값이 안 올랐어요.
examples.en: The stockpile was large enough that prices didn't rise.

examples.ko: 비상시를 위해 식량 비축에 신경 써요.
examples.en: I take care to stock up on food for emergencies.
Where do you keep the emergency food supply?
The drop in oil reserves was reported on the news.

explain: 나중에 필요할 때 쓰려고 물건을 모아 두는 것이라서 쌀, 석유, 식량 같은 말과 잘 어울려요. 돈을 모을 때는 '저축'을 쓰고, '비축 물량', '비축량'처럼 붙여서도 써요.
explain_en: It means keeping goods in store for later need, so it pairs with rice, oil and food. For money you use '저축', and it also forms compounds like '비축 물량' and '비축량'.

examples.en: I stock up on water and ramen in preparation for typhoons.
The government is stockpiling rice.
I stocked up on firewood in advance to get through the winter.
Keeping emergency food in stock gives me peace of mind.
I went to bed early today to save up my energy.
I'm worried because there isn't enough space to store supplies.

explain: 돈은 '저축하다', 물건이나 에너지는 '비축하다'로 구분해요. '힘을 비축하다'처럼 비유로도 쓰고, 일상 대화에서는 '쟁여 두다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: Money is '저축하다', while goods and energy are '비축하다'. It can be used figuratively, as in '힘을 비축하다', and in casual talk people also say '쟁여 두다'.

examples.en: It's exam season, so the atmosphere in the library is tense and grim.

examples.ko: 두 사람 사이가 살벌해서 말을 못 걸었어요.
examples.en: The mood between the two was so hostile that I couldn't talk to them.
Prices have risen brutally these days.
He stared at me with a fierce look, and I was scared.
The mood in the meeting was really harsh.
I heard the rent in this neighborhood is brutal.

explain: 분위기, 눈빛, 말투가 차갑고 적대적이라 긴장될 때 써요. '무섭다'와 달리 서로 맞서는 긴장감이 있고, 말할 때는 '살벌하게 비싸다'처럼 강조하는 말로도 써요.
explain_en: It describes an atmosphere, look or tone that is cold and hostile, creating tension. Unlike '무섭다', it carries a sense of confrontation, and in speech it can also be an intensifier, as in '살벌하게 비싸다'.

examples.ko: 이 서사시는 한 영웅의 일생을 노래해요.
examples.en: This epic poem sings of the life of a hero.
I gave a presentation about epic poetry in class.
The main character in the epic crosses the sea.
This movie feels like a modern-day epic.
Korea also has works known as epic poems.
Some people memorize long epic poems.

explain: 문학 수업에서 '서정시'와 짝으로 배우는 말이에요. 규모가 크고 웅장한 영화나 이야기를 칭찬할 때 '서사시 같다'라고 비유하기도 해요.
explain_en: You learn it in literature class as a pair with '서정시' (lyric poetry). People also use '서사시 같다' to praise a grand, large-scale film or story.

examples.ko: 그 분야의 석학이 강연을 하러 오셨어요.
examples.en: A leading scholar in that field came to give a lecture.
World-renowned scholars gathered in one place.
He is called a great scholar of economics.

examples.ko: 석학의 조언을 듣고 연구 방향을 바꿨어요.
examples.en: I changed the direction of my research after hearing a great scholar's advice.

examples.ko: 석학 초청 특강이 다음 주에 있어요.
examples.en: There is a special lecture by an invited scholar next week.
The students met the great scholar in person and asked questions.

explain: '학자'는 중립적인 말이고, '석학'은 학식이 아주 깊은 학자를 존경하는 마음으로 부르는 말이에요. 보통 '경제학계의 석학'처럼 분야와 함께 쓰고, 자기 자신에게는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: '학자' is neutral, while '석학' is a respectful term for a scholar of great learning. It is usually paired with a field, as in '경제학계의 석학', and you never use it about yourself.

examples.en: Old thermometers had mercury inside.
Mercury is a metal that is liquid at room temperature.

examples.ko: 수은 체온계가 깨지면 조심해서 치워야 해요.
examples.en: If a mercury thermometer breaks, you have to clean it up carefully.

examples.ko: 바다 생선의 수은 농도가 뉴스에 나왔어요.
examples.en: The mercury level in ocean fish was on the news.
The light of the mercury lamps lit up the street brightly.
I heard fish can be contaminated with mercury.

explain: 체온계 이야기에서 많이 듣는 금속 이름이에요. 독성 때문에 '수은 중독', '수은 오염'처럼 환경과 건강 뉴스에도 나오고, 가로등 이름 '수은등'에도 들어 있어요.
explain_en: It is the metal you hear about most in talk of thermometers. Because it is toxic, it also appears in environment and health news as '수은 중독' and '수은 오염', and it is part of the word '수은등' (mercury lamp).

examples.en: My grandmother is a kind-hearted and warm person.

examples.ko: 어진 임금 이야기를 역사 시간에 배웠어요.
examples.en: We learned a story about a benevolent king in history class.

examples.ko: 그 선생님은 성품이 어질어서 학생들이 잘 따라요.
examples.en: That teacher has a gentle character, so the students follow her well.

examples.ko: 어질게 살면 복을 받는다고 부모님이 말씀하셨어요.
examples.en: My parents said that if you live kindly, you will be blessed.
A person known for being gentle got angry.
All the people in that village are kind and gentle.

explain: '어진 사람'처럼 'ㄴ' 앞에서 'ㄹ'이 빠져요. '착하다'보다 너그럽고 덕이 있는 느낌이라 어른이나 임금을 칭찬할 때, 옛이야기에서 주로 쓰고, 요즘 대화에서는 '착하다'나 '마음이 넓다'를 더 많이 말해요. '어지럽다'와는 전혀 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: The 'ㄹ' drops before 'ㄴ', as in '어진 사람'. It feels more generous and virtuous than '착하다', so it is used to praise elders or kings and in old tales, while in modern talk people more often say '착하다' or '마음이 넓다'. It is a completely different word from '어지럽다' (dizzy).

examples.ko: 이 정수기는 여과 장치가 세 단계예요.
examples.en: This water purifier has a three-stage filtration system.
After filtration, the water becomes much cleaner.

examples.ko: 여과 필터는 석 달마다 바꿔야 해요.
examples.en: You have to replace the filter every three months.

examples.ko: 그는 생각을 여과 없이 말해서 가끔 오해를 받아요.
examples.en: He says what he thinks without any filter, so he is sometimes misunderstood.

examples.ko: 여과가 잘 안 되면 물이 탁해요.
examples.en: If the filtering doesn't work well, the water looks cloudy.

examples.ko: 커피는 여과 방식에 따라 맛이 달라요.
examples.en: Coffee tastes different depending on the filtering method.

explain: 물이나 공기를 거르는 일이지만, 말과 정보를 걸러 낼 때도 비유로 써요. 일상에서는 '거르다'라고 하고, '여과 없이'는 생각이나 말을 그대로 드러낼 때 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 그의 발언이 여과 없이 방송에 나갔어요.
phrases.en: His remarks were aired without any editing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말이나 영상을 다듬거나 걸러 내지 않고 그대로 드러낼 때 써요. 좋게도 나쁘게도 쓰지만 뉴스나 글에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when words or footage are shown as they are, without being polished or screened. It can be positive or negative and often appears in news and writing.

explain_en: It refers to filtering water or air, but it is also used figuratively for filtering words and information. In everyday speech people say '거르다', and '여과 없이' is common for showing thoughts or words just as they are.

examples.en: This machine filters the dust out of the water.
If you strain the broth through a cloth, it becomes clear.
I bought a mask that filters the air.
The filter is purifying the rainwater.
I drink the coffee after filtering it.
It's a vacuum cleaner that can filter out dust.

explain: 기계나 실험, 정수 이야기에서 쓰는 격식 있는 말이고, 일상에서는 '거르다'를 많이 써요. 정보나 말에도 '여과해서 듣다'처럼 비유로 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is a formal word used for machines, experiments and water purification, while everyday speech prefers '거르다'. It can also be used figuratively for information or words, as in '여과해서 듣다'.

examples.en: This video is not suitable for elementary school students.

examples.ko: 수업 시간에 본 영상물이 아주 인상적이었어요.
examples.en: The video we watched in class was very impressive.
You can borrow videos from the library.
You must not upload illegal videos.

examples.ko: 영상물 등급에 따라 볼 수 있는 나이가 달라요.
examples.en: The age you need to be to watch differs by video rating.
Our company makes educational videos.

explain: 영화, 드라마, 유튜브 영상을 한꺼번에 가리킬 때 쓰는 말로 법, 공문, 학교 이야기에서 자주 보여요. 친구와 말할 때는 그냥 '영상'이나 '동영상'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It covers films, dramas and online videos all at once and shows up in laws, official documents and school settings. When chatting with friends, people just say '영상' or '동영상'.

examples.ko: 한 번 이겼다고 자만하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't get overconfident just because you won once.

examples.ko: 그는 성공한 뒤에 자만해서 친구를 잃었어요.
examples.en: After succeeding, he became conceited and lost his friends.
Don't get cocky, and do your best until the end.

examples.ko: 자기 실력만 믿고 자만한 나머지 연습을 안 했어요.
examples.en: He trusted only his own skill and grew so overconfident that he didn't practice.

examples.ko: 자만하는 태도는 팀에 도움이 안 돼요.
examples.en: A conceited attitude does not help the team.
He got cocky about being first and lost in the final.

explain: 자기 능력을 과신해서 우쭐해지는 마음 상태를 말해요. 남에게 말로 '자랑하다'와 달리 마음가짐을 가리키고, '자만심', '자만에 빠지다'처럼도 써요. 영어 'show off'처럼 행동으로 뽐내는 뜻은 약해요.
explain_en: It describes the mental state of overestimating your own ability and becoming smug. Unlike '자랑하다', which is telling others, it points to your mindset, and it appears in '자만심' and '자만에 빠지다'. It is weaker than English 'show off' in the sense of displaying through actions.

examples.ko: 올림픽 성화 점화 장면은 늘 감동적이에요.
examples.en: The lighting of the Olympic torch is always moving.

examples.ko: 차의 점화 장치가 고장 나서 시동이 안 걸려요.
examples.en: The car's ignition system is broken, so it won't start.
The moment it was ignited, flames shot up.

examples.ko: 점화가 잘 안 되면 가스레인지가 켜지지 않아요.
examples.en: If ignition doesn't work well, the gas stove won't turn on.

examples.ko: 개막식 점화를 맡은 선수가 누구인지 궁금해요.
examples.en: I wonder who the athlete lighting the flame at the opening ceremony is.
When I pressed the ignition button, the fire lit up.

explain: 불을 붙이는 일이라서 성화, 엔진, 가스 기구 이야기에 나와요. 일상에서는 '불을 붙이다'라고 하고, '점화 장치', '성화 점화'처럼 다른 말과 붙여서 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is the act of setting something alight, so it appears with torches, engines and gas appliances. In daily speech people say '불을 붙이다', and it often forms compounds like '점화 장치' and '성화 점화'.

examples.en: When the athlete lit the torch, applause poured in.
Be careful when you light the burner.

examples.ko: 로켓 엔진을 점화한 지 몇 초 만에 떠올랐어요.
examples.en: The rocket lifted off just seconds after the engine was ignited.
I tried to light the candle with a lighter.
Check safety first, and then light it.
A loud noise came the moment it was ignited.

explain: 성화, 엔진, 버너처럼 불을 붙여 작동시키는 것이 목적어로 와요. 일상에서는 '불을 붙이다'나 '불을 켜다'라고 말하고, '점화하다'는 설명서나 뉴스에서 더 자주 보여요.
explain_en: Its objects are things lit to start working, such as torches, engines and burners. In daily life people say '불을 붙이다' or '불을 켜다', and '점화하다' appears more in manuals and news.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 와서 제방이 무너질까 걱정이에요.
examples.en: It's raining a lot, and I'm worried the embankment will collapse.

examples.ko: 강 제방을 따라 산책하는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people walk along the river embankment.

examples.ko: 제방에 구멍이 생겨서 물이 새고 있어요.
examples.en: A hole formed in the levee, and water is leaking out.
Cherry blossoms bloomed along the embankment road.
They started embankment construction to prepare for floods.
I can see people fishing on top of the embankment.

explain: 강이나 바다의 물을 막으려고 쌓은 둑을 말해요. 일상에서는 '둑'이라고 많이 하고, 뉴스나 공사 이야기에서는 '제방이 터지다', '제방이 무너지다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is a bank built to hold back river or sea water. In daily talk people often say '둑', while news and construction reports use phrases like '제방이 터지다' and '제방이 무너지다'.

examples.ko: 항아리 주둥이가 좁아서 물을 붓기 어려워요.
examples.en: The jar's mouth is narrow, so it's hard to pour water in.
The bird pecked at the insect with its beak.

examples.ko: 강아지가 주둥이를 내 손에 갖다 댔어요.
examples.en: The puppy put its snout against my hand.
Steam is rising from the spout of the kettle.

examples.ko: 주둥이 끝이 뾰족한 새를 본 적 있어요?
examples.en: Have you ever seen a bird with a pointed beak?

examples.ko: 병 주둥이를 입에 대고 마시지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't drink with your mouth on the bottle's opening.

explain: 새나 동물의 입 부분, 그리고 병이나 주전자처럼 좁게 튀어나온 입구를 가리킬 때 써요. 사람의 입에 쓰면 낮춰 부르는 말이라 무례하게 들리니 보통은 '입'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used for the mouth part of birds and animals, and for the narrow opening or spout of bottles and kettles. Using it for a person's mouth sounds rude and belittling, so people normally say '입'.

examples.ko: 옛날에는 장사하는 사람을 천시하는 분위기가 있었어요.
examples.en: In the past, there was an atmosphere that looked down on merchants.
You must not look down on any occupation.
He is a person who doesn't look down on labor.
You shouldn't look down on people because of their appearance.
There was an era when people looked down on others for their low status.
They looked down on craftsmen before, but now they respect them.

explain: '무시하다'보다 신분, 직업, 일 자체를 천하다고 낮게 보는 느낌이 강해서 역사나 사회 이야기에서 잘 나와요. '천대하다'와 가깝고, 반대 느낌의 말은 '존중하다', '중시하다'예요.
explain_en: Compared with '무시하다', it stresses seeing a person's status, job or work itself as lowly, so it fits history and social topics. It is close to '천대하다', and its opposites are '존중하다' and '중시하다'.

examples.ko: 요즘 학교는 시험보다 체험 활동에 치중해요.
examples.en: These days schools focus more on hands-on activities than on exams.
If you lean too much to one side, the balance breaks.
This shop put more weight on quality than on price.
The English study is focusing heavily on speaking.
I hope the class doesn't focus too much on grammar.
Ads that focus only on looks are not popular.

explain: 'A에 치중하다'처럼 조사 '에'와 함께 써요. 여러 가지 중에서 한쪽에 비중을 더 두는 것이고, 너무 쏠렸다는 부정적인 느낌이 들 때도 많아요. '집중하다'는 정신을 한곳에 모으는 것이라 달라요.
explain_en: It takes the particle '에', as in 'A에 치중하다'. It means putting more weight on one side among several things, and often carries a feeling of leaning too far. It differs from '집중하다', which is gathering your attention on one thing.

examples.en: We passed through a boundless plain by train.
Mongolia has many wide plains.
A herd of horses galloped across the plain.
The sunset seen from the plain is really beautiful.
I want to visit the North American plains.
Plains are good for farming.

explain: 산이 거의 없이 넓고 평평한 땅이에요. '평야'와 비슷한 말이고, '평원'은 탁 트인 넓은 풍경을 말할 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is wide, flat land with almost no mountains. It is close to '평야', and '평원' suits descriptions of open, far-reaching scenery.

examples.en: The Nobel Peace Prize winner was announced.
He gave a speech after receiving the peace prize.
There is an organization nominated for the peace prize.
This year's peace prize went to a human rights activist.
I heard he donated the peace prize money to people in need.
Please explain the meaning of the peace prize.

explain: 대부분 '노벨 평화상'이라는 이름으로 뉴스에 나와요. '평화상을 받다', '평화상을 수상하다'처럼 쓰고, 받은 사람은 '평화상 수상자'라고 해요.
explain_en: It mostly appears in the news as the '노벨 평화상' (Nobel Peace Prize). You say '평화상을 받다' or '평화상을 수상하다', and the recipient is the '평화상 수상자'.
